title: SDLC Workflow Local Configuration
description: Optional per-project configuration for sdlc-workflow view rendering, bootstrap, serve, and hook behavior. Store at .ai/sdlc-config.json.

artifactTracking.description: Whether the .ai/ workflow artifact tree is committed to git ('tracked') or gitignored except ship-plan.md + sdlc-config.json ('ignored'). Recorded once by /wf ship-plan init Step 3.5 so handoff/ship's clean-tree handling reads a policy instead of deciding ad hoc mid-release. Absent = policy unset (status surfaces a one-time advisory; ship asks per-run).

checks.description: How the write-time checks act. strict: a write that fails a gate is refused. warn: the write stands, and the same reason shows as a warning. off: no check runs. The lints only warn, in strict and warn alike.

semantic.description: Semantic leak guards (HOOKS-SEMANTIC Phase 1): the leak-guard-bash and leak-guard-write hooks scan outward-facing text (git commit/tag messages, gh pr/release titles+bodies, README/CHANGELOG/docs writes) for internal workflow vocabulary, using the lexicon derived from skills/wf/reference/_output-boundary.md. Default OFF and advisory-first; promote mode to 'enforce' only after the advisory false-positive rate proves ~0 across real workflows.

enabled.description: Master switch for both leak guards. Default false (the hooks exit silently).

mode.description: 'advisory' emits a non-blocking systemMessage naming the matched vocabulary; 'enforce' denies the tool call (exit 2) with the same message.

solutions.description: Knowledge-compounding corpus (INTENT-FIDELITY W12 meta-loop). `.ai/solutions/` is always the per-repo corpus; globalDir optionally adds a user-level one.

globalDir.description: Absolute path to a USER-LEVEL solutions corpus read by plan's reuse scan alongside the repo's .ai/solutions/, and the target for retro's user-confirmed lesson promotion + the about-the-workflow plugin-feedback.md channel. null (default) disables it. The dir stays local — never synced by the plugin, since repo lessons can contain project specifics (privacy).

models.description: The model of each stage agent of the /wf yolo driver. A stage names any model that the host can run: an alias (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`) or a model id, for example `claude-fable-5-1`. A stage that is not named runs on Opus, the default. Read at launch and passed in the driver args.

implement.description: The implement stage agent. The A/B of 2026-10-16 passed Sonnet here.

memory.description: Agent memory-file seeding (MEMORY-SEED-PLAN). Governs whether the SessionStart hook seeds a minimal, versioned `/wf` rules kernel into the repo's agent memory files. The kernel lives literally in AGENTS.md (canonical; read by Codex natively and by Claude via an `@AGENTS.md` import the seeder adds to CLAUDE.md). The plugin owns EXACTLY the fenced region and never touches a byte outside it; seeding only runs in sdlc-engaged repos (those with .ai/workflows/).

seedRules.description: When true (default), each SessionStart ensures the fenced `/wf` rules block in AGENTS.md and the `@AGENTS.md` import in CLAUDE.md, replacing an older kernel version in place and never re-announcing after the first insert. Set false to disable seeding entirely (existing seeded blocks are left untouched).

yolo.description: The /wf yolo watch (YOLO-COMMENTARY-PLAN). scripts/yolo-watch.mjs reads these settings when it starts.

protectedFiles.description: Repo-relative paths that the watch hashes every 20 seconds. A change gives a protected-change event and a push notification. PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, and every file with uncommitted edits when the run starts are always protected.

records.description: How the project links to the records repo of this machine.

project.description: The name of the project in the records repo. With records.repo in ~/.sdlc/config.json, it turns on the GitHub layer.
What the first-run setup recorded about the repo.

about.description: What the repo is, in one line from the person.

testProfile.description: The test suites of the project and their times. Intake estimates them without a run. A slice runs the fast and affected suites only; the full and heavy suites run once per packet, after the review fixes. The time box of a stage agent comes from these times.

budget.description: The check budget of the repo, chosen once by the person: how long a check may take before an agent moves it or makes it faster.

preset.description: The option that the person chose. fast-loop: slice checks up to 120 s, a long run up to 1 h. balanced: slice checks up to 600 s, a long run up to 1 h. thorough: no limit.

slice.description: The longest check that a slice stage may run, in seconds. A longer command is a long run. Null: the time box of the stage is the limit.

long.description: The longest single long run, in seconds, before the agent must offer the faster paths. Null: no limit.

machines.description: The machines that the person allows for split runs, by name.

setAt.description: When the person chose the budget.

devices.description: The devices that verify may drive. Verify uses an emulator or a simulator by default, and never drives a device that is not named here.

test.description: The ids of the physical devices that are for testing, for example an adb serial or a simulator UDID.

suite.description: One test suite of the project: the command that runs it, the estimate of intake, and the last measured time.

command.description: The command that runs the suite. For the affected suite, `{files}` stands for the changed files.

estimateSeconds.description: The time that intake estimates for one run, without a run.

measuredSeconds.description: The time of the last real run. It replaces the estimate. `wf.mjs profile record` writes it.

measuredAt.description: When the last real run ended.
